Shameless Snacks · Meta · static images · Jan 2023 to Nov 3, 2026

The 100 best images, all time

Ranked by the margin each image earned above an average image running in the same months, so a Black Friday ad doesn't win just for running in November. 224 images spent $2k or more; 148 beat their months' average; these are the top 100.

The 100 spent $2.15M at 0.78 CM-ROAS, against 0.62 for average images in the same months and 0.64 for all images ever. Together they earned +$346.8k more margin than average images would have on the same spend. Tap any image or code for the full file.

Read this first

The best images sell the sale, not the snack.68 of the 100 carry a discount, a per-bag price, free gifts or a deadline. They earned 64% of the extra margin ($220.8k of $346.8k), at 0.91 CM-ROAS against 0.69 for their months. 37 of the 41 images that paid for themselves after ad cost are deal images, and 40 of those 41 started between September 2025 and March 2026.
The biggest images are proof, not deals.Target sightings, the haul photo, the flavor game, the stat duel and the guilt-free bag: 19 images, $1.18M of spend, beating their months by a thinner edge (0.66 vs 0.55). Deal images rarely got big: the median deadline image spent $3.6k. #1, Final Clearance Sale, is the exception at $171.1k.
Appetite alone doesn't sell.3 of the 9 big images that ran below average are macro close-ups with no deal and no number: $253.2k at 0.41 against 0.56. They pulled the highest click rates of any big image (up to 3.2%) and the dearest orders ($99 to $124). All 3 macro shots that made the top 100 carry a sale strip.
Most of this list is history.70 of the 100 stopped running before July 2026, and only 14 started after the candy-first switch. The shapes transfer; many of the lines don't. The guilt-free bag line, weight-loss promises, body-transformation headlines and "real fruit" are off-limits now, and reusing any pre-June-2026 asset as-is goes through Legal.

What to make next

  • Deadline banner on Mini Bites and the variety packs. Yellow and red banner, a real-looking box stack, one reason: final clearance, last 2 pallets, inventory almost gone. The deadline family made money after ad cost as a group (+$10.1k on $395.4k), and the version with the 46% + 4 free gifts strip beat the same headline without it (#44 vs #98). The reason is the product here, so give every run a new one.
  • A Mini Bites founder letter. The goodbye letter beat its months 8 of 8 times and paid back 7 of 8; dressed as an Instagram post it hit 2.08 ROAS (#21). The same letter is the best big CTV video (SH-13396-1). A launch needs its own reason: a signed note from Paul & Giancarlo announcing the drop, in the black-letter or Instagram-post dress.
  • A Mini Bites haul. 28 mini bags tipped onto a kitchen table next to the box, no text. The haul photo is the biggest single image ($176.1k), and its October 2026 recut (#69) still beats its months.
  • Guess which flavor isn't ours, with the 16 Mini Bites flavors and one fake. The game scaled to $136.4k and makes people look at every bag.
  • Every macro shot gets a number or a deadline in frame. The bare macros ran below average on $253.2k; the same hearts with a sale strip made the top 15 (#13, #15). That's the brief for the macro retros off SH-17273-9.
  • Re-line the old proof winners instead of retiring them. "The whole bag is 70 calories" for the guilt-free bag (#2), "MOMS! THE WHOLE BAG IS 70 CALORIES" (#25), "FROM 184 CALORIES TO 70" for the dad-bod duel. Same layout, today's line.

Source. ejam-dwh.production.creative_dashboard, brand SHA, channel facebook, asset_type IMAGE, every day from Jan 12, 2023 to Nov 3, 2026. All images: $4.97M spend. One card is one design: 8 cards combine identical re-uploads or size versions of the same design (noted on the card). Video thumbnails filed as images were removed. Images with less than $2k spend are left out.

Ranking. "vs avg image" = the image's margin minus what an average SHA image would have made on the same spend in the same months. The average excludes the image itself and is weighted by the image's own monthly spend. CM-ROAS = (revenue + upsell - COGS - merchant fees - agency fees) / ad spend; 1.0 = breakeven after ad cost.

Money. Contribution = revenue + upsell - COGS - ad spend - agency fees - merchant fees (eJam Goal Pacing definition). CM % = contribution / revenue. Revenue is first-order attribution, so negative contribution is normal here; subscriptions pay back on rebills. ROAS = revenue / spend. Basket = revenue per order.

Labels. Families, deal flags and headlines come from reading each image, not from task names or AI tags. Built 2026-11-04 · rebuild: final.py then build_preview.py in projects/2026-11/sha-top100-images-alltime.
